lessons.claim: An integrated autocorrelation time measured on one observable must not be used to inflate another's error bar. Measured: tau_int of the mean particle height was 86-132 of 478 frames (N_eff 3.6-5.5), implying a 10x inflation, but the primary EOS statistic's own block SEM was 1.04x the independent-frame Monte Carlo -- h_mean tracks the slow drift on tau_fall = 9.35 tau_sed while the dense-region statistic decorrelates fast. Applying the 10x would have turned 15.6 sigma into 1.7 and killed an affordable campaign. The block SEM is itself a lower bound when tau_int exceeds the block length; the seed-to-seed spread is the error bar that matters.
